problems.title: A factorial quotient limit
problems.question: Evaluate the limit of (2n+3)!/[n²(2n+1)!] as n→∞.
problems.idea: Use exact formulas and retain every domain, sign and existence condition.
formulas: Cancel factorials, then divide by n².
steps: The expression is (2n+3)(2n+2)/n²=(2+3/n)(2+2/n), which tends to 4.
problems.note: The printed date says 7 March 2021 although the archive places this quiz in 2021–2022. Its archive placement is retained.

problems.title: A sine-exponential limit at zero
problems.question: Find the limit as x→0 of (sin x·eˣ−7x)/(4x²+8x).
problems.idea: Use exact formulas and retain every domain, sign and existence condition.
steps: For x≠0 divide by x to obtain [(sin x/x)eˣ−7]/(4x+8). The limit is (1−7)/8=−3/4.

problems.title: Derivatives by the chain rule
problems.question: f(x)=cos5x+(2x−3)⁶−199. Find f′(x).
problems.idea: Use exact formulas and retain every domain, sign and existence condition.
steps: The cosine term differentiates to −5sin5x. The sixth power gives 6(2x−3)⁵×2. The constant differentiates to zero.

problems.title: A decreasing interval determines a cubic coefficient
problems.question: f(x)=2x³+3x²−ax+6 has decreasing interval [−5,4]. Find a.
problems.idea: Use exact formulas and retain every domain, sign and existence condition.
formulas: f′(x)=6x²+6x−a; the interval endpoints are its zeros.
steps: Having zeros −5,4 forces f′(x)=6(x+5)(x−4)=6x²+6x−120. Comparing constants gives a=120.
The derivative is negative between the endpoints and positive outside, verifying the exact interval.

problems.title: Continuity at a removable hole
problems.question: f(x)=(x³−x²)/(x−1) for x≠1 and f(1)=cos alpha. Find all alpha making it continuous.
problems.idea: Use exact formulas and retain every domain, sign and existence condition.
formulas: For x≠1 the quotient equals x², whose limit at 1 is 1.
steps: Continuity requires cos alpha=1. This occurs exactly at alpha=2kπ.

problems.title: A formal fixed point is not the actual iteration limit
problems.question: a₁=x and aₙ₊₁=x^(aₙ). Find a real exponential-base x for which aₙ→199.
problems.idea: Use exact formulas and retain every domain, sign and existence condition.
formulas: A finite positive-base limit L must satisfy L=xᴸ, but this condition alone is not sufficient.
steps: The required limit would force x=199¹/¹⁹⁹. This candidate is >1 and satisfies x²<2, since 199²<2¹⁹⁹.
Inductively every term lies between 1 and 2: the first does, and if 1<aₙ<2, then 1<x^(aₙ)<x²<2.
The sequence therefore cannot converge to 199. Bases x≤0 do not give the standard real-exponent iteration needed here; x=0 fails at the next zero exponent.
problems.answer: No admissible positive real base x.
problems.note: Simply solving 199=x¹⁹⁹ produces a fixed-point candidate that the given starting value never approaches. The bounded-iteration check rules it out.

problems.title: Coordinate triangle area
problems.question: A=(1,3),B=(−3,5),C=(−5,2). Find area ABC.
problems.idea: Use exact formulas and retain every domain, sign and existence condition.
formulas: Area=half the absolute 2D determinant of AB,AC.
steps: AB=(−4,2),AC=(−6,−1). The determinant is 4+12=16, so area=8.

problems.title: Cylinder area from a lateral-to-base ratio
problems.question: A cylinder’s lateral area is twice one base area and its axial-section area is 8. Find total surface area.
problems.idea: Use exact formulas and retain every domain, sign and existence condition.

problems.title: Insphere of a rotated right triangle
problems.question: A 3,4,5 triangle rotates about its hypotenuse line. Find the radius of the sphere inscribed in the resulting double cone.
problems.idea: Use exact formulas and retain every domain, sign and existence condition.
formulas: The common cone-base radius is altitude 3×4/5=12/5. In an axial section, sphere tangency becomes a circle tangent to the four kite sides.
steps: Let its centre lie distance t from the endpoint whose adjacent leg is 3. Its distances to the two cone-side lines are (4/5)t and (3/5)(5−t).
Equate them: 4t=15−3t, so t=15/7. The common distance is 12/7, the sphere radius.

problems.title: Four tangent spheres stacked in a cylinder
problems.question: Four pairwise tangent spheres each have surface area 16π. Three touch one cylinder base and its lateral surface; the fourth touches the other base. Find cylinder height.
problems.idea: Use exact formulas and retain every domain, sign and existence condition.
formulas: 4πr²=16π gives r=2. Sphere centres form a regular tetrahedron of edge 4, height 4√(2/3).
steps: The lower centre plane is 2 above the bottom. The upper centre is a tetrahedron height above it; the top cylinder base is another radius 2 above.
